notes: §1985:IX.4.8.4 GR2: "Within a declarative procedure, there must be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures"; it is a general rule with no stated consequence, so by §1985:I.1.6 ("The results of violating the formats or rules of Standard COBOL are undefined unless otherwise specified") a 1985 compiler need not refuse it, and 1985 has no RESUME exception to admit. Every procedure-name operand goes through ProcedureTableBuilder.ResolveProcedureOperand into StatementValidation.CheckDeclarativesBoundary, which at --std 85 reports the violation as warning COBOL2375 and compiles (determination docs/CONFORMANCE.md D-DECLREF, the at-85 paragraph); RESUME is refused at 85 by the edition gate (COBOL0876). Probes at --std 85 (classes b,c): PERFORM P-2, PERFORM P-2 THRU P-3 (two warnings), GO TO P-2, PERFORM of the nondeclarative section, ALTER P-SW TO PROCEED TO P-3 (two warnings) each warn COBOL2375 and run; RESUME NEXT STATEMENT refused COBOL0876; the witness's PERFORM and GO TO of declarative paragraphs compile with no diagnostic and print the USE procedure lines. The warning text quotes §2023:14.9.49.3 SR3 (with its RESUME exception) at 85 rather than the 1985 rule, a wording point, not a behavior one.

next.reason: 1985: "Within a declarative procedure, there must be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures."; 2023: "there shall be no reference to any nondeclarative procedures except in a RESUME statement.". Same prohibition, but 2023 adds an exception allowing a RESUME statement in a declarative to reference a nondeclarative procedure, a case the 1985 rule did not allow.
